tweets: High in the Himalayas, water drips onto rock and freezes into a pillar of ice that swells and shrinks with the moon — nobody builds it, nobody carves it. ❄️

This is the Amarnath cave, perched near 3,888m in the Kashmir Himalayas. Meltwater seeping through the limestone roof freezes layer by layer into a natural ice stalagmite pilgrims venerate as a Shiva lingam.

The site isn't a modern find — Kashmir's ancient Nilmat Purana already names it a sacred tirtha. Legend holds that here Shiva revealed the secret of immortality to Parvati, and two pigeons who overheard became immortal — pilgrims report spotting pigeons near the cave.

The Amarnath Yatra ranks among the world's highest pilgrimages: trekking from Pahalgam or Baltal through glacier passes to reach a cave near 12,756 feet. Every Shravan (July-August), lakhs of pilgrims make the climb.
By autumn the ice lingam has melted away, only to re-form again next summer — the mountain rewriting the same story every year. Follow @yddoseOfHistory for your daily dose of history. 🙏
